summary: This wiki note summarizes Richard Hildebrandt, who led the SS Race and Settlement Main Office (RuSHA) from 1943 until his capture in 1945 and held the rank of SS-Obergruppenführer. He was convicted in the RuSHA Trial at Nuremberg for germanization measures under the Generalplan Ost in the Danzig-West Prussia area, including resettling Germans after expelling native families. As RuSHA chief he also oversaw racial testing of occupied territory populations for selection, and he was executed for war crimes.
one_line: Richard Hildebrandt was an SS-Obergruppenführer who led the RuSHA, convicted at the Nuremberg RuSHA Trial and executed for war crimes.
key_facts: Richard Hildebrandt led the SS Race and Settlement Main Office (SS-Rasse und Siedlungshauptamt; RuSHA) from 1943 until his capture in 1945.
Richard Hildebrandt held the rank of SS-Obergruppenführer.
Richard Hildebrandt was convicted in the RuSHA Trial, a phase of the Nuremberg trials.
The RuSHA Trial convicted Richard Hildebrandt for measures carried out in furtherance of the germanization component of the Generalplan Ost program.
The germanization measures for which Richard Hildebrandt was convicted took place in the Danzig-West Prussia area.
The germanization measures involved resettling Germans in Nazi-occupied territory after ejecting the native families from those lands.
As RuSHA chief, Richard Hildebrandt was responsible for conducting the official Race test on the population of the occupied territories for racial selection.
Richard Hildebrandt was executed for war crimes.
